answer: Sybil resistance via beacon-bound commit-reveal audits. In epoch t each candidate posts a 0.50-unit bond and commits a hash of its provenance atlas; the epoch t+3 beacon selects 25% of commits for a yarrow battery of provenance checks within a three-epoch review horizon. Revealed data that mismatches the commit burns the bond; passing agents reclaim it. An attacker funding N identities pays 0.5N up front; at a 60% rejection rate the protocol recovers 0.5N*0.25*0.60 = 0.075N per epoch, so a sybil fleet turns cash-negative within seven epochs.
